section: Linguistic groups of India - language families, Eighth Schedule languages, bilingualism
subsections: Language families - languages and share of speakers; tribal languages (Halbi, Ho, Kui, Mundari)
Most spoken languages - speaker ranking in India, world ranking of Indian languages

accepted.s: Which language family accounted for approximately 73 per cent of India's speakers according to the older figures used in APPSC material?
accepted.x: The Indo-European or Indo-Aryan family accounted for approximately 73 per cent of speakers in the older figures. The 2011 Census estimate was about 78.05 per cent.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive numerical share to separate the major language families.
accepted.sec: Language families - languages and share of speakers; tribal languages (Halbi, Ho, Kui, Mundari)

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the major language families of India:
1. Indo-Aryan languages are concentrated mainly in northern, western and eastern India.
2. Dravidian languages account for about 20 per cent of speakers in the older figures.
3. Austro-Asiatic languages account for about 20 per cent of speakers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false: Austro-Asiatic languages account for only about 1.1–1.4 per cent of speakers.
accepted.tq: Identify the wrong numerical statement by comparing the relative shares of language families.
accepted.sec: Language families - languages and share of speakers; tribal languages (Halbi, Ho, Kui, Mundari)

accepted.s: Which one of the following sets consists entirely of Indo-Aryan languages mentioned in relation to northern, western and eastern India?
accepted.x: Hindi, Bengali, Marathi and Gujarati are Indo-Aryan languages concentrated mainly in northern, western and eastern India.
accepted.tq: Classify a complete set by matching languages with their language family and region.
accepted.sec: Language families - languages and share of speakers; tribal languages (Halbi, Ho, Kui, Mundari)

accepted.s: The Dardic branch, including Kashmiri, belongs to which language family?
accepted.x: Kashmiri belongs to the Dardic branch of the Indo-Aryan family. Dardic is not a Sino-Tibetan branch.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the closely confused Dardic and Sino-Tibetan classifications.
accepted.sec: Language families - languages and share of speakers; tribal languages (Halbi, Ho, Kui, Mundari)

accepted.s:
With reference to the Dravidian language family, consider the following statements:
1. Telugu is classified as a South-Central Dravidian language.
2. Tamil, Kannada and Malayalam are associated with the southern branch.
3. Kui, Gondi and Kurukh are identified with Central or North Dravidian areas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Telugu is South-Central Dravidian, while Kui, Gondi and Kurukh represent Central or North Dravidian languages or pockets.
accepted.tq: Check each branch-language association before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Language families - languages and share of speakers; tribal languages (Halbi, Ho, Kui, Mundari)

accepted.s: The Austro-Asiatic language family in India is represented by which of the following branches?
accepted.x: The Austro-Asiatic family includes the Munda branch, with languages such as Santhali and Mundari, and the Mon-Khmer branch, including Khasi.
accepted.tq: Recall the two-branch structure of the Austro-Asiatic family.
accepted.sec: Language families - languages and share of speakers; tribal languages (Halbi, Ho, Kui, Mundari)

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Kui is a Dravidian language associated with the Kandhas of Odisha. Santhali, Khasi and Garo are correctly matched with their respective branches or families.
accepted.tq: Find the wrongly assigned language family among otherwise familiar tribal-language pairs.
accepted.sec: Language families - languages and share of speakers; tribal languages (Halbi, Ho, Kui, Mundari)

accepted.s: The Sino-Tibetan or Tibeto-Burman languages of India are concentrated mainly in which region?
o: The north-eastern States, Sikkim and Himalayan areas
The Deccan plateau and Tamil Nadu
The Konkan coast and western Rajasthan
accepted.x: Sino-Tibetan languages are concentrated in the north-eastern States, Sikkim and Himalayan areas, and are also represented in Ladakh and Himachal Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Use regional distribution to distinguish Sino-Tibetan languages from the other families.
accepted.sec: Language families - languages and share of speakers; tribal languages (Halbi, Ho, Kui, Mundari)

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Ho — Dravidian language of Tamil Nadu
accepted.x: Halbi is an Indo-Aryan language spoken in the Bastar region of Chhattisgarh. Kui is Dravidian, while Ho and Mundari are Austro-Asiatic Munda languages.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure regional association and eliminate the swapped family-location pairs.
accepted.sec: Language families - languages and share of speakers; tribal languages (Halbi, Ho, Kui, Mundari)

accepted.s: Kui or Kuvi is primarily associated with which community and language family?
accepted.x: Kui or Kuvi is a Dravidian language spoken by the Kandhas of Odisha. Khasi and Garo belong to different language groups.
accepted.tq: Link the tribal community, language and language family rather than relying on region alone.
accepted.sec: Language families - languages and share of speakers; tribal languages (Halbi, Ho, Kui, Mundari)

accepted.s: Santhali, Mundari and Ho belong to which branch of the Austro-Asiatic family?
accepted.x: Santhali, Mundari and Ho are associated with the Munda branch of the Austro-Asiatic family, especially in Jharkhand, West Bengal and Odisha.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Munda branch from the Mon-Khmer branch within Austro-Asiatic.
accepted.sec: Language families - languages and share of speakers; tribal languages (Halbi, Ho, Kui, Mundari)

accepted.s: The Ol Chiki script used for Santhali was created by whom and in which year?
accepted.x: Raghunath Murmu created the Ol Chiki script for Santhali in 1925.
accepted.tq: Combine the creator and year to avoid confusing a script fact with a general language fact.
accepted.sec: Language families - languages and share of speakers; tribal languages (Halbi, Ho, Kui, Mundari)

accepted.s: The presence of Khasi, an Austro-Asiatic language of the Mon-Khmer branch, is considered evidence that the Meghalaya plateau was once part of:
accepted.x: Khasi is treated as evidence that the Meghalaya plateau was once part of peninsular India. Its Mon-Khmer affiliation links it with the Austro-Asiatic linguistic zone.
accepted.tq: Apply a linguistic-distribution clue to infer the historical geographical relationship.
accepted.sec: Language families - languages and share of speakers; tribal languages (Halbi, Ho, Kui, Mundari)

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Santhali — Austro-Asiatic
2. Savara — Austro-Asiatic
3. Garo — Sino-Tibetan
4. Gor Boli — Indo-Aryan
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Santhali and Savara are Austro-Asiatic, Garo is Sino-Tibetan and Gor Boli is Indo-Aryan.
accepted.tq: Verify each tribal-language affiliation individually before choosing the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Language families - languages and share of speakers; tribal languages (Halbi, Ho, Kui, Mundari)

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the smaller language families of India is correct?
o: The Austro-Asiatic family accounts for nearly one-fourth of India's speakers.
The Andamanese or Semito-Hamitic group is represented by Andaman tribes and Arabic.
The Sino-Tibetan family is confined exclusively to peninsular India.
The Mon-Khmer branch consists only of languages spoken in Rajasthan.
accepted.x: The Andamanese or Semito-Hamitic group is a tiny group represented by Andaman tribal languages and Arabic. The other statements wrongly alter the share or geographical distribution.
accepted.tq: Reject absolute geographical claims and identify the precise composition of the minor group.
accepted.sec: Language families - languages and share of speakers; tribal languages (Halbi, Ho, Kui, Mundari)

accepted.s: According to the 2011 Census-based figures, which sequence correctly represents the approximate shares of Indo-Aryan, Dravidian, Austro-Asiatic and Tibeto-Burman languages respectively?
accepted.x: The approximate 2011 shares were Indo-Aryan 78.05 per cent, Dravidian 19.64 per cent, Austro-Asiatic 1.11 per cent and Tibeto-Burman 1.01 per cent.
accepted.tq: Read the figures in the stated order and distinguish the 2011 values from older estimates.
accepted.sec: Language families - languages and share of speakers; tribal languages (Halbi, Ho, Kui, Mundari)

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the older figures from the 2011 Census-based estimates for India's language families?
1. The older estimate for Indo-Aryan was about 73 per cent, whereas the 2011 estimate was about 78.05 per cent.
2. The older estimate for Dravidian was about 20 per cent, whereas the 2011 estimate was about 19.64 per cent.
3. The older estimate for Tibeto-Burman was about 20 per cent.
Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false: the older Tibeto-Burman estimate was about 0.85 per cent, not 20 per cent.
accepted.tq: Compare corresponding figures and detect the misplaced decimal-scale percentage.
accepted.sec: Language families - languages and share of speakers; tribal languages (Halbi, Ho, Kui, Mundari)

accepted.s:
Arrange the following Indian languages in descending order of their share of speakers according to the 2011 Census:
A. Telugu
B. Hindi
C. Tamil
D. Bengali
accepted.x: The correct order is Hindi (43.6 per cent), Bengali (8.0 per cent), Telugu (6.7 per cent) and Tamil (5.7 per cent).
accepted.tq: Order the items by their numerical shares, beginning with the largest value.
accepted.sec: Most spoken languages - speaker ranking in India, world ranking of Indian languages

accepted.s: According to the 2011 Census ranking given for India, which language occupied the third position in terms of speakers?
accepted.x: Marathi ranked third in 2011 with about 6.9 per cent of speakers. Telugu ranked fourth with about 6.7 per cent.
accepted.tq: Pay attention to the close Marathi–Telugu ranking and the changed position after 2001.
accepted.sec: Most spoken languages - speaker ranking in India, world ranking of Indian languages

accepted.s: Which change in the ranking of Indian languages occurred between the 2001 and 2011 Census figures?
o: Bengali moved from second to fifth, while Tamil became second.
Hindi moved from first to third, while Marathi became first.
Tamil moved from fifth to third, while Telugu became fifth.
Telugu moved from third to fourth, while Marathi overtook it for third place.
accepted.x: Telugu had occupied third place in 2001, but Marathi overtook it in 2011; Telugu consequently stood fourth.
accepted.tq: Test the direction of change in a close ranking rather than merely recalling the final order.
accepted.sec: Most spoken languages - speaker ranking in India, world ranking of Indian languages

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the world ranking of the three Indian languages mentioned among the world's most spoken languages?
accepted.x: Among the stated world rankings, Hindi is second, Bengali is seventh and Punjabi is tenth.
accepted.tq: Retain the separate world ranks and avoid substituting the Indian domestic ranking.
accepted.sec: Most spoken languages - speaker ranking in India, world ranking of Indian languages

accepted.s: Which language is described as the most spoken first language and as the lingua franca of northern and central India?
accepted.x: Hindi is the most spoken first language and functions as the lingua franca of northern and central India.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the status of a first language and lingua franca from a language's global rank.
accepted.sec: Most spoken languages - speaker ranking in India, world ranking of Indian languages

accepted.s: Approximately what proportion of Indians speak lesser-recognised local languages?
accepted.x: About 12 per cent of Indians speak lesser-recognised local languages.
accepted.tq: Recall the specific proportion rather than inferring it from the shares of major languages.
accepted.sec: Most spoken languages - speaker ranking in India, world ranking of Indian languages

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the ranking of languages in India and the world:
1. Bengali ranked second in India in the 2011 Census figures cited.
2. Bengali ranked seventh among the world's most spoken languages in the stated comparison.
3. Punjabi ranked tenth in the same world ranking.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: Bengali was second in India, seventh globally in the stated ranking, and Punjabi was tenth globally.
accepted.tq: Separate domestic rank from global rank while checking all three independently.
accepted.sec: Most spoken languages - speaker ranking in India, world ranking of Indian languages

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Bengali ranked second in India in 2011, not third. Marathi, Telugu and Tamil occupied the third, fourth and fifth positions respectively.
accepted.tq: Find the single reversed rank among a sequence of closely placed languages.
accepted.sec: Most spoken languages - speaker ranking in India, world ranking of Indian languages

accepted.s: A student identifies a language as South-Central Dravidian and places it among the four major southern languages listed with Tamil, Kannada and Malayalam. Which language has the student identified?
accepted.x: Telugu is classified as South-Central Dravidian. Tamil, Kannada and Malayalam are associated with the southern Dravidian group, while the other options belong to different families.
accepted.tq: Infer the language from its branch classification and neighbouring group description.
